notes:
\*\*This is the big one. Thank you for waiting.\*\*



I'll be straight with you: this release exists because a lot of the app needed rebuilding, and that was on me and you have been the people living with the consequences — the crashes, the stutter, the functions that just didnt do anything. You stuck with me through it anyway. That means a lot, and this update is what I have to show for it.



\---



\## The map now comes from my server — and it is rendered by D2R itself



This is the part I am most proud of, and I don't believe anyone else is doing it.



Until now, every map hack out there — mine included — has worked by reading the old Lord of Destruction files sitting on your PC. All using the old "Blacha" setup. Which in the end has been detected for ages. Or, they pinged an internal function, tricking the app (and leaving a trace).



\*\*All of that is gone.\*\* Your app now just asks my server for the map, and my server sends it back.



\- \*\*No LoD files.\*\* Nothing to download, nothing to install, nothing to keep in the right folder.

\- \*\*No extra .exe running on your machine.\*\* One less moving part, one less thing to go wrong, one less thing for your antivirus to argue with. One less thing for warden to see. 

\- \*\*The maps are generated from D2R itself\*\*, not from a decade-old copy of the game's data. They are the real thing.



The last point matters more than it sounds. Because the maps come from D2R, \*\*if Blizzard adds new areas, this keeps working.\*\* I am no longer tied to Lord of Destruction, so I am no longer one patch away from being broken.



Getting here meant reverse-engineering how D2R builds its maps, and that took a long time. The fragile part now lives on my machine instead of yours, which is exactly where it should be.



The old map hack had features this doesn't have yet. I will be bringing them back one at a time. If there is something you miss, \*\*submit a ticket\*\* — that list is genuinely how I decide what to do next.



One honest note: because the maps come from my server, you need to be online for them, and if my server has a bad day you'll feel it. I think that is a much better trade than the setup problems it replaces, but you should know it up front.



\---



\## Window layout, rebuilt



\*\*Your window positions now stick.\*\* Arrange your windows how you want them, press \*\*Save Positions\*\*, and that is where they will be — after a restart, after a reboot, forever, until you change them. Positions are remembered per account \*and\* per role, so the same account running as Main and as Filler keeps two different places.



\*\*Renderless actually does something now.\*\* It idles your non-Main, non-BoBarb windows out of the way between macros so they stop eating your GPU, and brings them back — one at a time, deliberately — when a macro starts. They never steal focus and never jump in front of your Main window. Press Stack or Spread whenever you want to see them again.



\*\*Spread respects your choices.\*\* If you have positioned and saved a window, Spread leaves it where you put it instead of tiling over the top of it.



\*\*Frameless windows are properly black\*\* now, instead of showing a pale border on some machines.



\---



\## A Help section that actually helps



New in the app: press \*\*Help\*\*, and there is a \*\*"Help me set up"\*\* guide that walks you through the whole thing in order — accounts, logins, mods, roles, teams, Quick Launch, first launch.



It is not a wall of text. Each step \*\*takes you to the right screen and highlights the actual button\*\*, while staying out of your way so you can click it. It also knows what you have already done and skips ahead to what you haven't, and it remembers where you got to if you close it.



There are guides for individual topics too, and a live list of your own hotkeys.



\---



\## Scaling



The app now follows the size of your display instead of assuming everyone runs the same screen I do. If it has been too small or too large for you, that should be sorted.



\---



\## Logins: back to what you know



I reverted to the login system you are familiar with. \*\*The app can pull tokens for you again, and you can paste your own token in.\*\* The version I tried in between was fine in principle but not good enough in practice, and I would rather ship the thing that works than defend the thing that was clever.



\---



\## Known issues — read this bit



\*\*Downloading my mods from inside the app does not work right now.\*\* For the moment, get your mods from \*\*Nexus Mods\*\* — there are good ones there. I will get back to mine, but it is honestly not near the top of my list, and I would rather tell you that plainly than leave a broken button and say nothing.



\---



\## Keep the tickets coming



Almost everything in this release came from something one of you reported or asked for. If it is broken, if it is missing, or if it is just annoying — \*\*open a ticket\*\*. It gets read.



Thanks for sticking around.
